clue.text: Plane number five is first

indicators.note: first says the five and the is come at the front, ahead of the number

parts.note: V is the Roman numeral for five
taken as written
to count is to number, and a count is a number reached

explanation.surface: A pilot announces that aircraft number five is first in line for take-off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first' is an indicator on the charade, putting the five and 'is' ahead of the number. The Vickers Viscount was a well-known British airliner of the 1950s.
explanation.definitionFit: The Vickers Viscount was a turboprop airliner, so the name stands for a kind of aircraft.

clue.text: Private war aim' encompassed by surgeon joining army

indicators.note: encompassed by means surrounded by, so the aim sits inside the surgeon

parts.note: a vet is an animal surgeon
an end is an aim or goal
TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve

explanation.surface: A personal feud whose goal is held by a doctor who has enlisted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'joining' is a link word placing TA after. The TA (Territorial Army) is Britain's part-time reserve force.
explanation.definitionFit: A vendetta is a feud pursued privately, often a blood feud between families.

clue.text: It's proper to embark before quiet take off

parts.note: to ship is to go or put aboard a vessel
sh is a call for quiet
to ape is to mimic, to take off

explanation.surface: It is correct to go aboard before a silent take-off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'take off' looks like departure but means impersonate. 'It's' and 'before' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: Shipshape means neat and in good order, as everything should be.

clue.text: Carrying weight, honours, with' a bridge, player

parts.note: OBEs are British honours (Officer of the Order of the British Empire)
in bridge the four players are North, South, East and West: E is East

explanation.surface: A heavy player at the bridge table, decorated with honours.
explanation.walkthrough: OBE is a British honour awarded by the monarch. 'with' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Obese means very overweight, carrying a lot of excess flesh.

clue.text: Heart of a tricky clue, in Greek characters

indicators.note: in places the rearranged letters inside the Greek letters

parts.note: nu is a letter of the Greek alphabet; two of them are nus

indicators.note: tricky suggests something twisted, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: The core of a hard clue lies in some Greek letters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tricky' rearranges the clue's letters to CLEU, and 'in' sets that among the Greek letters. 'Heart' looks like it means the middle of the clue, but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A nucleus is the central core around which something is built.

clue.text: What fans 'do when header goes astray

indicators.note: going astray means wandering off course, so these letters are set out in a new order

explanation.surface: Football supporters cling on loyally even when a headed shot goes wide.
explanation.walkthrough: 'goes astray' rearranges the letters of HEADER. 'fans' looks like football supporters cheering a header, and the definition plays on that: devoted followers stick to their team.
explanation.definitionFit: Devoted supporters stick by their cause, and to stick by something is the sense of the verb here.

clue.text: Refuse to believe in 'a black mark

explanation.surface: Someone will not trust a person with a stain on their record.
explanation.walkthrough: The verb means to disbelieve; the noun is a source of disgrace.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means to doubt or reject; as a noun it is a disgrace or blot on one's name.

clue.text: Wood chopped by one

indicators.note: chopped means cut up, so these letters are cut and reassembled

explanation.surface: Timber cut by a single person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'chopped' rearranges BYONE; the surface of a woodcutter hides the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: Ebony is a very dark, dense hardwood from tropical trees.

clue.text: What Gog and Magog do as a finale

explanation.surface: The legendary giants perform as a closing act.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer as three words: both names finish with the letter G. Gog and Magog are legendary giants of London lore.
explanation.definitionFit: Both names finish with the same letter, so they terminate on it; and a conclusion or close is a finale.

clue.text: Neglected to' give up.Times leader

parts.note: to forgo is to give up or do without

indicators.note: leader means the first letter of the following word

explanation.surface: A Times editorial failed to give something up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leader' looks like a newspaper editorial (a leader in British papers) but takes the first letter of Times. 'to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To have forgotten to do something is to have neglected it.

clue.text: Feature about one racket'

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the feature goes round the one

parts.note: the nose is a facial feature
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A news item about a single tennis bat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts I inside NOSE. 'racket' looks like a tennis bat but means a din.
explanation.definitionFit: A racket is a loud din, an unwelcome clamour of sound.

clue.text: Curse your occupation.

explanation.surface: Someone is told off for swearing at work.
explanation.walkthrough: A curse is a cross (angry) word; and filling in this puzzle is what the solver is busy with right now.
explanation.definitionFit: An angry oath is a cross word; and the solver is at present occupied with this very grid puzzle.

clue.text: Seasonal gift from the orient before a horse

parts.note: the orient is the east
ere is an old word for before
a gee-gee is a child's word for a horse, written GG

explanation.surface: A present from the Far East arrives ahead of a horse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from' and 'a' are link words. GG (gee-gee) is nursery talk for a horse.
explanation.definitionFit: A chocolate treat given at the spring festival is a classic present of the season.

clue.text: Right every time about fabric

parts.note: ay (or aye) is an old word meaning always, ever
on means about, concerning, as in a talk on art

explanation.surface: Correct, each time, about the cloth.
explanation.walkthrough: AY in the sense 'always' is an archaic, poetic usage.
explanation.definitionFit: Rayon is an artificial silk-like textile made from cellulose.

clue.text: Get Sara drunk — it'll make her cry

indicators.note: drunk means mixed up and unsteady, so these letters are tossed into a new order

explanation.surface: Ply Sara with drink and she will end up weeping.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drunk' rearranges GETSARA. The tears in the definition are the point of this irritant gas, used for riot control.
explanation.definitionFit: This riot-control gas irritates the eyes and makes anyone exposed weep.

clue.text: Maybe pear given' by this, or other fruit?

definitions.text: Maybe pear given' by this, or other fruit?

indicators.note: maybe suggests the letters could be arranged differently, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Could a plant produce pears or some other fruit?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Maybe' rearranges PEAR and GIVEN together; the whole clue then wryly asks if this plant might give a pear rather than its own fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: A grapevine is the climbing plant that bears grapes, a fruit.

clue.text: Barber left cut half way through for a stroll

parts.note: Sweeney Todd is the murderous barber of Victorian melodrama

indicators.note: cutting a word half way through keeps only its first half

explanation.surface: A barber stopped cutting midway and went out for a walk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut half way through' keeps LE, the first half of 'left'. Sweeney Todd, the demon barber of Fleet Street, is a figure of London legend and the musical.
explanation.definitionFit: A toddle is a short leisurely walk, an unhurried amble.

clue.text: Richard puts one pound on the roan by mistake

indicators.note: by mistake means things are set down wrongly, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
L stands for the pound sterling (Latin libra)

explanation.surface: Richard bets a pound on the roan horse by error.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by mistake' shuffles I, L and THEROAN. Richard I of England was nicknamed the Lionheart.
explanation.definitionFit: King Richard I was known as Coeur de Lion, the brave-hearted king.

clue.text: One way and another, accepting a criterion

indicators.note: accepting means taking in, so the a goes inside the ways

parts.note: ST is the abbreviation for street, a way
taken as written
RD, road, is another way

explanation.surface: Two routes alike, taking in a single measure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One way and another' gives two road abbreviations joined by 'and'; 'accepting' slips the A in just before the second way.
explanation.definitionFit: A standard is a benchmark or yardstick against which things are judged.

clue.text: It's heavenly being back in, the never-never land.., of metrication

indicators.note: back means the whole run of letters is read in the reverse direction

parts.note: the never-never is British slang for hire purchase, HP
an are is the metric unit of land area (100 square metres), plural ares

explanation.surface: An angel returns to the realm of hire purchase and metric land measures.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns HPARES round. HP, hire purchase, is the British name for buying on instalments, nicknamed 'the never-never'.
explanation.definitionFit: A seraph is one of the highest order of angels.

clue.text: Tramp around the North, but firstly have a chat

indicators.note: around means the tramp encloses the north

parts.note: a hobo is a tramp or vagrant
N is the abbreviation for north

indicators.note: firstly takes the opening letter of the next word

explanation.surface: A vagrant wandering the north stops first for a natter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' puts N in HOBO, and 'firstly' gives B from 'but'.
explanation.definitionFit: To hobnob is to mix socially and talk familiarly with others.

clue.text: Fire-walker's part in haste

explanation.surface: A fire-walker hurries across the coals.
explanation.walkthrough: A fire-walker's sole would be a hot foot; and to go hotfoot is to go in a hurry.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone crossing burning coals has a scorched sole; and the adverb means hurriedly, at speed.

clue.text: Harry caught that bird

parts.note: Hal is a nickname for Harry, as in Shakespeare's Prince Hal
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
yon is an old word for that, over there

explanation.surface: Harry caught that bird.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as a birdwatcher spotting a bird; the halcyon is the legendary kingfisher.
explanation.definitionFit: The halcyon is a mythical bird linked with the kingfisher, said to calm the seas.

clue.text: An awkward gait I had, that's clear.

parts.note: a limp is an awkward, uneven way of walking
I'd is the contraction of I had

explanation.surface: Someone admits to having walked with a limp, and says so plainly.
explanation.definitionFit: Limpid water is transparent, and limpid prose is lucid.

clue.text: So. fill this with money' when I'm sad

indicators.note: this answer with an extra letter put in gives the phrase for being sad, so the letter is taken away

parts.note: feeling blue is feeling sad, so I'm sad is I'm blue
L, for the pound (Latin libra), stands for money

explanation.surface: Someone stuffs their pockets with cash whenever they feel down.
explanation.walkthrough: Read backwards in logic: this word with L (money) added becomes I'M BLUE, 'when I'm sad'. So remove L from IMBLUE.
explanation.definitionFit: To imbue is to saturate or permeate, to steep something through.

clue.text: The boat for a bumping race?

definitions.text: The boat for a bumping race?

parts.words: The boat for a bumping race?
parts.note: bumping races are rowing contests at Oxford and Cambridge where crews chase and bump one another

explanation.surface: Asking which vessel suits a bumping race.
explanation.walkthrough: In British university bumping races, crews try to hit the boat in front. A heavy flat-bottomed boat that also means to shove into people fits wryly.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a flat-bottomed river boat, and the verb means to push or bump roughly, as racers do.

clue.text: Over priest's head, hairless, 'a place where hair may grow

parts.note: bald means hairless
a beard grows on the chin

explanation.surface: Above the bald priest's head, a spot where hair might sprout.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is descriptive: a baldachin is the canopy that stands over an altar, and so over the officiating priest's head.
explanation.definitionFit: A baldachin is an ornamental canopy raised above an altar or throne.

clue.text: Through having half. our capital in silver

indicators.note: in places the shortened capital inside the silver

parts.note: Ag is the chemical symbol for silver

indicators.note: half means three of the six letters of the capital city are dropped

parts.note: for a British paper our capital is London

explanation.surface: Having just half of London in silver bars.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half' keeps the first three letters of the capital, and 'in' puts them inside the silver symbol. A British paper's 'our capital' is London.
explanation.definitionFit: Along means through the length of something, as in walking through or along a street.

clue.text: Frugality is standard ecclesiastic malpractice

parts.note: par is the standard or norm
simony is the buying or selling of church offices

explanation.surface: Thrift is said to be the norm among corrupt clergy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is' is a link word. SIMONY, named after Simon Magus, is trading in church posts.
explanation.definitionFit: Parsimony is extreme thrift, stinginess with money.

clue.text: All right with it in a foreign city

indicators.note: in places the it within the all right

parts.note: OK means all right
it means sex appeal, abbreviated SA

explanation.surface: Fine, along with some charm, in a city abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it' as sex appeal (SA) is an old crossword convention. Osaka is a major Japanese city.
explanation.definitionFit: Osaka is a large port city in Japan.

clue.text: Dredge river enclosure

parts.note: the Dee is a river in Wales, England and Scotland
a pen is an enclosure for animals

explanation.surface: Dredging a river pound.
explanation.walkthrough: The Dee is a British river (there are ones in Wales/Cheshire and in Scotland).
explanation.definitionFit: Dredging scoops out a channel bed and makes the water lower-floored, giving it more depth.

clue.text: Honoured King, late Fleet Street worker

parts.note: K is the chess abbreviation for king
night is the late part of the day
Fleet Street was London's newspaper district; ED is an editor

explanation.surface: A king honours a late-shift newspaper journalist.
explanation.walkthrough: A night editor works the late shift on a paper; Fleet Street was the home of the London press.
explanation.definitionFit: To be given a knighthood is to be honoured by the sovereign with a title.
